title: Stanford Undergraduate to Face Trial on Rape Charges in Dorm Assault Case
excerpt: Leo Rossitter, 24, a Stanford economics and data science student, was charged in October 2024 with rape of an intoxicated person and two other counts after a fellow student alleged he assaulted her in her dorm room. A hearing to schedule the trial is set for December.
content:
A Stanford University undergraduate will face a criminal trial in Santa Clara County on charges that he raped a fellow student in her dorm room, according to public court filings reported by The Stanford Daily.

Leo Rossitter, 24, an economics and data science student, was charged in October 2024 by the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office with rape of an intoxicated person, oral copulation of an intoxicated person and penetration by force. A hearing to schedule the trial is set for December.

According to court filings cited by The Daily, the alleged assault happened in the fall of the woman's sophomore year. She said Rossitter offered to walk her back to her dorm after a party while she was visibly drunk, then allegedly tried to kiss her repeatedly before climbing onto her bed and sexually assaulting her.

Stanford's Title IX process took about two years to conclude and determined, based on a preponderance of credible evidence, that Rossitter committed sexual assault, The Daily reported. He received a two-year suspension and became eligible to return to campus this fall quarter. The university confirmed he is enrolled and living off campus while taking classes.

The woman, a former student, declined to comment. Last month she published an op-ed in The Daily under the name "A Stanford Jane Doe" criticizing what she described as slow responses and poor coordination between Stanford, the district attorney's office and law enforcement.

Rossitter's attorney, Daniel Barton, said his client "is not guilty of the horrible things that he is accused of." The Title IX finding is a university determination, not a criminal conviction. Rossitter has not been convicted of any crime, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

Rossitter, who entered Stanford as a member of the Class of 2025, currently works as a business strategist for the NBA's Minnesota Timberwolves, according to his LinkedIn profile. He was not publicly identified in news coverage until The Daily's report this week.

Sources: The Stanford Daily, Nov. 11, 2026; New York Post, Nov. 12, 2026.
